items.title: US business activity cools in October; strong demand fueling price pressures By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US business activity slowed modestly in October, though robust demand allowed companies to raise prices for goods and services, a sign that inflation could increase further and remain persistently high in the coming months. S&P Global said on Friday its flash US Composite PMI Output Index, which tracks the manufacturing and services sectors, slipped to 57.6 this month from a five-year high reading of 58.4 in September. A reading above 50 indicates expansion in the private sector. Strength in manufacturing was offset by a slight pullback in the vast services sector. The PMI suggested the economy started the fourth quarter on solid footing following what is expected to have been a strong performance in the July-September quarter. Economists expect the government’s advance gross domestic product report next week to show the economy growing at around a 3.0% annualized rate last quarter, mainly driven by consumer spending and business investment in AI. The economy has so far not shown any signs of buckling under the weight of the oil price shock stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran, with savings, generous tax returns in the spring, tariff refunds, a strong stock market performance and corporate profits providing a cushion. Economists warned that the inflation fallout from the drawn-out Middle East conflict was likely to slow consumer spending this quarter. ... Its gauge of prices for output rose to 59.8, the highest reading since August 2022, from 58.4 in September. Businesses across manufacturing and services sectors raised prices. Delivery performance by suppliers to manufacturers deteriorated further. The survey’s measure of suppliers’ delivery times dropped to a more than four-year low of 38.1 from 40.9 in September. SUPPLY BOTTLENECKS INTENSIFYING ... "Cost pressures remain a key concern," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence. "Supply chain bottlenecks have meanwhile intensified, and order book backlogs are growing, making it easier for companies to pass higher costs on to customers." ... Consumer and producer prices increased strongly in September, the government reported this month, raising concerns that inflation was fanning out across the economy. The Federal Reserve in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range. ... Economists expect the US central bank to stand pat at its meeting next week and hike borrowing costs again in December.

items.title: Obama is set to campaign with Democrats in Ohio and ...
items.excerpt: Barack Obama will campaign Saturday with Democratic candidates for the U.S. Senate in Ohio and Michigan, both highly competitive states that will help determine control of the chamber, as the former president ramps up his involvement in the midterm elections. Obama's first event is in Cleveland with former three-term Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown, who is looking to unseat Republican Sen. Jon Husted. Amy Acton, a Democrat running for governor against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, will also appear at the rally. Although Ohio has become more reliably Republican, it's been a hotly contested battleground this year. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both visited the state in recent weeks to drum up support for Husted and Ramaswamy. Obama then heads to a rally in Detroit for Abdul El-Sayed, a former public health official who is working to unite the Democratic base in Michigan after winning a divisive primary by less than a percentage point. El-Sayed is running against former Rep. Mike Rogers, a Republican. Obama’s appearance in the city, which is three-quarters Black, could bolster support for El-Sayed among Black voters. In the primary, his opponent Haley Stevens won Wayne County, which includes Detroit, by about 6 percentage points. Former Vice President Kamala Harris, the first Black and South Asian vice president, campaigned for El-Sayed in September. ... Michigan also has open races for governor, attorney general and secretary of state. Jocelyn Benson, the Democratic nominee for governor, is slated to appear along with others down the ballot. Benson is running against Republican Rep. John James.

For another family friendly option to watch this weekend, Peacock just got "Finding Emily," a delightful dose of nostalgia for anyone who grew up in the golden age of rom-coms.
